name: hybrid-generalizability
title: What decomposing the hybrid solver into processes adds, and what it costs
description:
Builds on cosim-vs-embedded-hybrid. Every study reuses the same HybridModel and
partitioner and changes one component at a time:

- the PDE engine (numpy finite volume vs FEniCSx),
- the PDE discretization of a curved domain (VCell Cartesian/staircase vs body-fitted P1),
- the splitting scheme (lagged Jacobi as in fvsolver, Gauss-Seidel, Strang),
- optionally, the particle engine.

at_a_glance.role: FEniCSx PDE process on a mesh matched to the FV grid; separates discretization error from coupling error.
A ball discretized as a body-fitted P1 mesh coupled through a background grid; to be compared with native VCell on the same analytic sphere.
Fields next to the membrane; native VCell on pyvcell's smoothed grid vs co-sim on the body-fitted mesh.
Removes the co-sim's boundary artifact (mesh membrane) and fixes curved-compartment creation in the Smoldyn fork.
Co-sim on VCell's own geometry (staircase PDE, smooth membrane); the accessible-volume correction makes it unbiased and conservative.
One non-convex GeometryDescription through native VCell, the co-sim on VCell's geometry and the Netgen co-sim; the correction removes VCell's −18–26% exchange loss.
Lagged Jacobi vs Gauss-Seidel vs Strang splitting; accuracy vs cost.
Phase 6; the A3 hybrid written to SBML Spatial with species representations and run from it on both solvers, seed-for-seed identical to the original runs.
The same composite with the PDE engine (and optionally the particle engine) swapped.
Stretch goal, membrane-bound particles and surface actions with panel-indexed binning.

question: Once the co-simulation reproduces the embedded hybrid solver, what does expressing the method as interchangeable processes add (alternative PDE discretizations, alternative splitting orders, swappable engines), and what do those choices cost in accuracy and performance compared with VCell's own discretization of the same problems?
hypothesis: Swapping the finite volume PDE process for a FEniCSx process changes results only by the PDE discretization error. A body-fitted unstructured mesh is an alternative discretization of curved domains, which VCell itself handles with a Cartesian volume grid and tangent-plane/Voronoi membrane numerics; the two should agree to discretization error. Higher-order splitting (Strang) reduces the coupling error at modest extra cost. vcell-fvsolver's hybrid loop (SimTool.cpp) implements one fixed splitting order, so trying another there means changing the solver.

executive.what_is_this: A study of the generality gained by decomposing the hybrid solver into process-bigraph processes.

studies.name: fenicsx-same-problem
studies.title: PDE engine swap, FV (VCell FV_SOLVER scheme) vs FEniCSx Q1 under the same coupling
studies.question:
Can the PDE half of the co-simulation be swapped for a different discretization
(FEniCSx, Q1 finite elements) without changing anything else, and does that change the
coupled result beyond discretization error?

studies.name: unstructured-geometry
studies.title: Hybrid co-simulation with a body-fitted unstructured PDE mesh (ball)
studies.question:
Can the co-simulation use a body-fitted unstructured mesh for the PDE half of a curved
domain, as an alternative to VCell's own Cartesian volume grid with staircase-membrane
numerics, while keeping the particle ↔ field handoff conservative and accurate?

studies.name: sphere-cosim-vs-native
studies.title: Same ball, two discretizations: native VCell (Cartesian + membrane numerics) vs co-simulation (body-fitted P1)
studies.question:
On a curved domain (a ball), how do the native VCell hybrid and the co-simulation compare?
- Native VCell uses analytic geometry on its Cartesian volume grid: the membrane is a
  staircase geometrically, but numerically uses local tangent-plane projections and
  Voronoi neighbours.
- The co-simulation uses a body-fitted P1 mesh coupled through a background grid.

studies.name: near-membrane-fields
studies.title: Fields next to a curved membrane: native VCell on pyvcell's smoothed grid vs co-sim on a body-fitted mesh
studies.question:
B2b found that the native hybrid loses molecules at the curved membrane. Where does that
show up in the field, and does the co-simulation have its own boundary artifact?
Native fields are read on pyvcell's smoothed unstructured grid, so boundary elements sit
near the true membrane rather than on the staircase.

studies.name: cosim-boundary-transfer
studies.title: Removing the co-simulation's boundary artifact: particle transfer, membrane geometry and curved-compartment creation
studies.question:
B2c found the co-simulation's ensemble-mean B 1.3% too high in the outer shell of the ball.
Two causes were candidates:
- the two-stage particle transfer (nearest grid node, then Pᵀ to mesh DOFs);
- the domain mismatch: Smoldyn's exact sphere holds about 1.4% more volume than the
  inscribed P1 mesh.
Which is it, and what does removing it cost?

studies.name: vcell-geometry-cosim
studies.title: The co-simulation on VCell's own geometry: staircase PDE, smooth membrane, accessible-volume correction
studies.question:
Native VCell solves the PDE on the voxel staircase but confines particles by a smooth membrane.
For the B2b ball the two domains differ by ~1.8% in volume. That leaves a −1.4% outer-shell
depletion and an exchange drift, even with the binning correction of vcell-fvsolver#25
(Study B2c). With the co-simulation running on exactly VCell's geometry, can an
accessible-volume correction make the coupling both unbiased and conservative?

studies.name: dumbbell-three-ways
studies.title: One non-convex GeometryDescription, three solver paths: native VCell, co-sim on VCell's geometry, co-sim on a Netgen mesh
studies.question:
Phase 7e end to end on a non-sphere: does one geometry description drive the native VCell solver
and both co-simulation paths, and do the accessible-volume correction and the body-fitted mesh
stay unbiased and conservative on a thin-necked, non-convex shape?

studies.name: splitting-schemes
studies.title: Operator-splitting schemes for PDE/particle coupling: Jacobi (fvsolver), Gauss–Seidel, Strang
studies.question:
The embedded vcell-fvsolver hard-codes one lagged (Jacobi-type) splitting. With the
coupling expressed as process-bigraph processes, can other splittings be used, and how
much accuracy do they buy at a given coupling interval?

studies.name: sbml-spatial-hybrid
studies.title: The hybrid model described in SBML Spatial, run on both solvers
studies.question:
Can a PDE/particle hybrid be described in SBML Spatial, with each species' representation
(continuous or particle) as a VCell annotation, and run unchanged from that SBML on both
the native VCell solver and the co-simulation?
